content.text:
Make this game with Mesh Control Engine through this MCP server, with no human in the loop:

A short 2D platformer. Moth, lanterns, bats, moon gate.

Work in this order and check each step before the next:
1. Read mce://docs/guide/14-mcp-ai-workflow.md (the tools and the workflow) and mce://docs/guide/README.md. Call engine_capabilities to see what is data (components, assets, MCP tools) and what needs game code.
2. Find the closest worked sample or example with docs_search ("platformer", "visual novel", "3d kit") and read its scene and code under mce://docs/samples/ or mce://docs/examples/.
3. Components and systems the game needs that the engine lacks go in the game module: edit it, then module_build (errors come back as file:line:col) and module_test.
4. Author the scenes with entity_create / component_set, save with scene_save, verify with run_headless (inspect, trace) and look with render_frame after every visible change.
5. Write .mctest scenarios under tests/ (a walk_to bot that must finish each level, no log errors) and run them with test_run; use playtest's feel report (stuck spots, deaths, idle time) to fix levels.
6. Keep goldens of the title and each level with image_diff, so later changes that break a screen show up.
7. Finish: a title, win and lose, credits for every asset (CREDITS.md; gen_* and library_add write the rows), project_check until pass is true, then ship_build (mce://docs/guide/15-shipping.md has the rest).

# 14. Working with an AI agent (MCP)

Every project has an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server (`<game>_mcp` from the checkout build, or
the stock `mce_mcp --module <lib<game>.so>`, `mce mcp` with the SDK) that gives an AI agent
the same scene-editing commands a person has in the editor, plus cook and headless verification.
Three games in the repository were authored entirely this way (Kindle's level, Prism Break and
Undertow), and a fourth (Lamplighter) by an agent that had never seen the engine source. This
chapter is the workflow that worked and the pitfalls it found.

## 14.1 Starting the server

```sh
build/<preset>/projects/MyGame/my_game_mcp --project projects/MyGame
build/<preset>/projects/MyGame/my_game_mcp --project projects/MyGame --scene scenes/main.mcscene
build/<preset>/projects/MyGame/my_game_mcp --project projects/MyGame --allow-cheats
build/<preset>/src/editor/mcp/mce_mcp --module build/<preset>/projects/MyGame/libmy_game.so --project projects/MyGame
mce mcp MyGame                                      # the SDK: the line above with its own paths
```

The server speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin and stdout, one message per line (the MCP stdio
transport); it opens no socket. Stdout carries nothing else: logs go to stderr, and so does the
command line `mce mcp` prints before it starts the server. Use the **project's** server or the stock one **with the module**:
without `--module`, `mce_mcp` knows only the engine's components (the visual-novel kit's included) and r [... 28179 characters cut]

# Kindle

The UC-D proof game (ROADMAP M9, `docs/milestones/M9-ucd.md`): one small 2D level made with the
MCE project template and the project editor's MCP server. It reuses Ember Step's mechanics (the
platformer controller, coins, spikes, the goal flag, crumbling blocks, a moving platform) as authored
components, and adds one mechanic: **colour switches**. Touching a switch swaps which block colour
is solid. Red starts solid; the red wall needs the first switch, the blue bridge over the pit needs
it too, and the red stairs to the flag need the second.

Controls: A / D or the arrows run, Space jumps (again off a wall), J dashes, Esc pauses, ` opens the
console. Gamepad: left stick / d-pad, A, X.

contents.text:
# 11. Input

Gameplay never sees keys, buttons or SDL events. Each fixed tick the engine folds every device
event into one immutable snapshot, `input::InputState`, and your systems read that. The snapshot
is part of the determinism contract: it can be recorded and replayed, and the same snapshot
sequence gives the same game.

## 11.1 Reading input

```cpp
void player(Frame& f) {
    const input::InputState& in = f.resource<input::InputState>();
    const f32 mx = in.move.x;                 // -1..1, WASD / arrows / left stick / d-pad
    if (in.jump_pressed) { ... }              // edge: this tick only
    if (in.jump_held) { ... }                 // level
    if (in.fire_pressed) { ... }
    if (in.pause_pressed) { ... }
    const bool dash = in.has_action(MCE_SID("Dash")) ? in.pressed(MCE_SID("Dash")) : in.fire_pressed;
}
```

| Member | Action | Default bindings |
|---|---|---|
| `move` (vec2) | Move | W A S D, arrows, left stick, d-pad |
| `look` (vec2) | Look | mouse delta, right stick |

arguments.summary: No run-time scene change, and a game module cannot reach the asset system to do one itself
arguments.expected: a data or code way to go from one scene to the next (title -> level 1 -> level 2 -> win/lose), e.g. a SceneChange event or request resource the player acts on
arguments.actual: guide 4.5: no built-in scene switching at run time; scene::load needs an asset::AssetSystem, and guide 6.10 says the template host does not hand it to the module
arguments.workaround: read the AssetSystem pointer from kit::SequenceRegistry::assets() (install_stock sets it), load_sync the Scene, destroy every entity of every World table through Commands and ecs::load_scene inside FixedUpdate_Pre (recorded as Commands)
arguments.details: every multi-level game made from the template needs this; the workaround relies on an unrelated resource

tools.name: refl_list_components
tools.description: List every reflected component type (name and field count).

tools.name: refl_describe_component
tools.description: Describe a component type, or a reflected value type such as UiAnchors or UiStyle (runtime UI): fields with kind, array count, nested struct fields, enum values, editor range, read-only/transient flags and help text.

tools.name: scene_info
tools.description: The open scene: name, GUID, path under assets/, unsaved changes, entity count.

tools.name: scene_list_entities
tools.description: List the scene's entities in file order: id, name, component types. Optional component filter.

tools.name: scene_get_entity
tools.description: One entity (by id, or by name when unique) with its component values in .mcscene form (fields at their default are omitted; entity references are "$<id>"). Ids are saved in the file and survive scene_open.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: asset_list
tools.description: Assets of the project (GUID registry): guid as "guid:<uuid>", path under assets/, type.

type.description: Texture, Font, Sfx, Scene, Mesh, Material, ...

tools.name: asset_set_import_settings
tools.description: Replace an asset's importer settings in its .mceasset sidecar (texture: {"srgb": bool, "mips": bool}; a normal map or LUT needs srgb false). Keys are validated by the next cook_run.

tools.name: entity_create
tools.description: Create an entity (with a LocalTransform unless transform is false) and optionally components, e.g. {"Sprite": {"texture": "guid:...", "size": [1, 1]}}. With 'prefab', an instance of that .mcprefab whose 'components' override the prefab root's fields (LocalTransform places it). Returns its id.

prefab.description: "guid:<uuid>" of a .mcprefab: place an instance; components then override the prefab root's fields

at.description: Index in the hierarchy; default: the end

tools.name: entity_delete
tools.description: Delete an entity (references to it become null).

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: scene_clear
tools.description: Delete every entity of the open scene (one undo step): re-author a scene keeping its GUID and path.

tools.name: entity_duplicate
tools.description: Duplicate an entity right after itself. Returns the new id(s).

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: component_add
tools.description: Add a component (default values, or patched with 'value': an object of fields).

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: component_remove
tools.description: Remove a component from an entity.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: component_set
tools.description: Change a component. Without 'path', 'value' is an object of fields to change. With a property path ("position", "position.x", "shape.half", "items[2]"), 'value' is that property's value. Type errors name the expected type.

entity.description: Entity id, or its name when unique

tools.name: scene_new
tools.description: Start a new, empty, unsaved scene (refuses to drop unsaved changes unless force).

tools.name: scene_open
tools.description: Open a .mcscene, or a .mcprefab to edit the prefab itself (entity 0 is its root), by its path under assets/ (refuses to drop unsaved changes unless force).

tools.name: scene_save
tools.description: Save the scene (atomic write; entity ids are saved with it). With 'path' (under assets/): save as, with a fresh GUID for a new file. 'name' renames the scene. When another agent saved the file since it was opened, their edits are merged in entity by entity; edits to the same component of an entity conflict and nothing is written unless resolve picks a side. Refuses to overwrite another existing file unless force (an overwritten file keeps its GUID; force skips the merge). A path ending in .mcprefab saves the document as a prefab (entity 0 is the root; prefab_create_from makes one from an entity).

tools.name: scene_undo
tools.description: Undo the last scene edit (one tools/call is one step; editor edits share the history).

tools.name: scene_redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone scene edit.

tools.name: cook_run
tools.description: Cook the project (incremental) into <project>/cooked. pack: also write <project>/assets.mce (a host built from the project plays its own build-tree pack unless started with -pack <that file or the cooked dir>). adopt: give new source files (a PNG, WAV or TTF added under assets/ with no .mceasset sidecar) a sidecar with a fresh GUID instead of a cook error. Returns counts, diagnostics with file:line and the output paths (relative to the project folder).

tools.name: cook_errors
tools.description: Diagnostics of the last cook (file, line, col, stage, message).

tools.name: asset_delete
tools.description: Delete a source file under assets/ together with its .mceasset sidecar (not the open scene). The catalog is rescanned.

tools.name: run_headless
tools.description: Cook, then play the saved scene headless for N fixed ticks exactly as the game's host plays it with -headless (the game's own systems included in a project server), or another saved scene of the project with 'scene'. Returns the World state_hash (same scene + ticks + input = same hash), World metrics and the log tail. input: scripted keyboard/gamepad actions per tick, as the game reads them from InputState ("Move" [x,y], "Jump", "Fire", "Pause", "Confirm", "Cancel" and any game-defined action name); a press is a one-tick segment, a hold a range. inspect: after the last tick, report the live component values (Transient runtime fields included) of scene entities by id and/or of every entity with a component (at most 64); show picks the components to print. trace: component fields of scene entities every N ticks, as series (how a value moved over the run, not only where it ended).

scene.description: Play this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one; inspect then takes 'component' only

input.description: Either a script string, one segment per line: "<from>[-<to>] Action[=value] ..." (e.g. "10-70 Move=1,0 Jump\n100 Fire"), or an array of segments

actions.description: Action name -> true, a number, or [x, y]

component.description: Every live entity with this component (also ones the run spawned)

show.description: Components to print (default: the entity's scene components, or the filter component + LocalTransform)

trace.description: Sample fields during the run: {"every": ticks (10), "fields": [{"entity": id or name, "field": "LocalTransform.position.x"}]} (at most 16 fields, 1000 rows)

tools.name: console_list
tools.description: List console variables (type, value, flags, help) and console functions. Optional name prefix.

tools.name: console_exec
tools.description: Execute one console line ("name" prints, "name value" sets, "func args" calls). Cheat and restart-only variables are refused unless the server runs with --allow-cheats.

tools.name: render_frame
tools.description: See the game: draw the open (saved) or another saved scene with the real player at sim tick N, with scripted input, from its own camera or another, at a chosen size and safe area. Returns the frame as a PNG image. Works without a GPU (offscreen software rendering). 'save' also writes the PNG under the project folder.

tick.description: Capture the first frame after this sim tick

scene.description: Render this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one

input.description: Scripted input as run_headless takes it: a script string ("10-70 Move=1,0 Jump") or an array of {from, to, actions}

camera.description: Render from another camera (render only, the sim is unchanged): {"entity": id or name} of a camera entity in the open scene, {"index": n} (scene entity index), {"position": [x,y,z], "target": [x,y,z], "fov": deg} (free 3D) or {"center": [x,y], "zoom": z} (free 2D)

safe_area.description: Pretend the screen has these safe-area insets in pixels {left, top, right, bottom}: UI lays out inside them and the image outlines them

software.description: Force the offscreen software renderer (automatic when there is no display)

save.description: Also write the frame as a PNG at this path inside the project folder, e.g. shots/title.png

tools.name: render_sheet
tools.description: A contact sheet: frames at several ticks (columns) from one or more cameras (rows) in one image, each cell labelled with its tick. One player run per camera.

cameras.description: Camera objects as render_frame's 'camera'; default: the scene's own

scene.description: Render this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one

input.description: Scripted input as run_headless takes it: a script string ("10-70 Move=1,0 Jump") or an array of {from, to, actions}

camera.description: Render from another camera (render only, the sim is unchanged): {"entity": id or name} of a camera entity in the open scene, {"index": n} (scene entity index), {"position": [x,y,z], "target": [x,y,z], "fov": deg} (free 3D) or {"center": [x,y], "zoom": z} (free 2D)

safe_area.description: Pretend the screen has these safe-area insets in pixels {left, top, right, bottom}: UI lays out inside them and the image outlines them

software.description: Force the offscreen software renderer (automatic when there is no display)

tools.name: image_diff
tools.description: Compare a frame with a golden PNG in the project: 'image' (a PNG in the project) or 'render' (render_frame's arguments). Returns the score (mean channel difference, 0..1), the changed fraction and pass (score <= max_score), with a heat map image. With no golden yet, or update: true, the image becomes the golden.

golden.description: PNG path inside the project folder, e.g. goldens/title.png

image.description: PNG path inside the project folder to compare

render.description: render_frame arguments: the frame to compare

tick.description: Capture the first frame after this sim tick

scene.description: Render this saved scene (path under assets/) instead of the open one

input.description: Scripted input as run_headless takes it: a script string ("10-70 Move=1,0 Jump") or an array of {from, to, actions}

camera.description: Render from another camera (render only, the sim is unchanged): {"entity": id or name} of a camera entity in the open scene, {"index": n} (scene entity index), {"position": [x,y,z], "target": [x,y,z], "fov": deg} (free 3D) or {"center": [x,y], "zoom": z} (free 2D)

safe_area.description: Pretend the screen has these safe-area insets in pixels {left, top, right, bottom}: UI lays out inside them and the image outlines them

software.description: Force the offscreen software renderer (automatic when there is no display)

threshold.description: Channel difference a pixel may have and still count as unchanged

update.description: Write the image as the new golden

tools.name: module_build
tools.description: Rebuild the game module with the project's CMake build (the tree the loaded module came from) and map the new build into this server: new and changed components and systems are live for the next tool call, no restart. Returns the compiler's errors (and with warnings: true its warnings) as {severity, file, line, col, message}, plus the output's end when the build failed. The open scene is kept (re-read with the new layouts); the undo history restarts.

reload.description: Map the new build after a successful build

tools.name: module_test
tools.description: Run the project's tests with ctest in the module's build tree (default filter: tests named <game>_*, such as the <game>_headless_300 smoke test). Returns each test's result and the output's end when one failed.

tools.name: test_run
tools.description: Run playtest scenarios without a person: .mctest files (JSON) under the project's tests/ folder, one file or folder ('path'), or one inline scenario ('test'). A scenario plays a saved scene headless with scripted input or a built-in bot, may stop early ('until'), and checks component fields (at the end or at a tick), entities alive, event counts, the log and the bot's feel metrics. Returns each scenario's checks with actual values, its state_hash, and the feel report (time to finish, deaths, stuck spots, idle time) when it has an actor.

path.description: A .mctest file or a folder of them inside the project (default tests/)

test.description: One scenario inline, in the .mctest format: {name, scene, ticks, input | bot, actor, until, death, assert: [checks], trace}

tools.name: playtest
tools.description: Let a built-in bot play the scene and say how it felt: walk_to (head for a point or entity, jumping or sidestepping when stuck), explore (seeded random wandering, coverage) or masher (random button chords, crash and soft-lock hunting). Returns the feel report: time to finish, deaths, stuck spots with positions, idle time, distance, cells visited. Needs no game code: the bot drives the game's input actions (Move, Jump, ...).

bot.description: {kind: walk_to|explore|masher, actor: entity, target: [x,y(,z)] or entity (walk_to), plane: xy|x|xz (default xy; x = side view with Jump, xz = 3D ground), reach: m (0.5), seed, move: action (Move), jump: action (Jump), actions: [names] (masher), period: ticks (8)}

scene.description: A saved scene under assets/ (default: the open scene)

until.description: Stop early when this check holds (a field, alive or event check)

death.description: Count a death each time this check becomes true, e.g. {entity, field: Health.hp, <=: 0}

trace.description: {every: ticks, fields: [{entity, field}]}: sample fields during the run

tools.name: docs_search
tools.description: Search the engine's shipped docs (user guide, engine reference), the worked samples and the example games. Returns the best sections with their mce://docs/... resource URI, heading, line and a snippet; read the whole file with resources/read. Start with mce://docs/index.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "camera shake" or "RigidBody2D"

tools.name: engine_capabilities
tools.description: What a game reaches through what: each engine feature with how it is reached today (data: a component; asset: a source file type; mcp: a tool; console; code: needs game C++), plus every component, importable asset type, tool and the convar count. Read this before planning a game, to keep game code to the rules.

area.description: Only this area's features (2D, 3D, physics, audio, input, ui, gameplay, scenes, agent, ...)

tools.name: gen_palette
tools.description: Generate a color palette (dark to light) from a seed and a scheme: analogous, complementary, triad, pastel, earth, neon or mono. Returns the colors as hex with a swatch image. 'save' writes it as a 1-pixel-high PNG strip under assets/.

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_sprite
tools.description: Generate pixel-art sprites: a mirrored, outlined, shaded creature, character, ship, item or blob from a seed, in 'colors' (hex, dark to light, at least 3; the darkest outlines) or a palette 'scheme'. 'variants' puts that many (seeds seed, seed+1, ...) in one row. Returns the frames' rects and an enlarged preview. 'save' writes the PNG under assets/ (nearest filtering, no mips) with its sidecar and a CREDITS.md row.

scheme.description: Palette scheme when 'colors' is not given (gen_palette's)

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_tileset
tools.description: Generate a pixel-art tile set in one row: fill, fill_2, fill_3 (variations), top, top_left, top_right (surface edges), platform and decoration. Styles: grass, stone, brick, dirt, sand, snow, water, wood, metal. Returns each tile's rect and a preview; 'save' writes the PNG under assets/ for a TileMap's tile set.

colors.description: 4 fill colors dark to light, or 4 fill + 3 surface colors (default: the style's)

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_texture
tools.description: Generate a noise texture (value, perlin, fbm, ridged, worley; tileable by default) mapped through 'colors' gradient stops, or an equirect sky (kind sky: horizon, zenith and cloud colors, 'clouds' cover, 'stars' density; width = 2 x height) for a skybox or a backdrop. 'save' writes the PNG under assets/ (linear filtering, mips).

colors.description: Gradient stops low to high (sky: horizon, zenith, clouds)

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_sfx
tools.description: Generate a retro sound effect with an sfxr synthesizer: a preset (pickup, laser, explosion, powerup, hit, jump, blip, random) varied by the seed, with any sfxr parameter overridden in 'params'. Returns the parameters used (tweak and call again), the length and level, and a waveform image. 'save' writes a 16-bit WAV under assets/.

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

tools.name: gen_music
tools.description: Generate a seamless music loop (bass, chords, melody and optional drums) in a scale on a root note, exactly 'bars' bars of 4 beats at 'bpm', at most 60 seconds. Returns its length and a waveform image; 'save' writes a 16-bit WAV under assets/ (set the AudioSource to loop).

save.description: Also write the result under assets/ at this path (with its .mceasset sidecar and a CREDITS.md row), e.g. sprites/slime.png

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (its GUID is kept)

arguments.summary: module_build reports reloaded:true but the server keeps the old module: every reload copies to the same libglowmoth_loaded_<pid>_0.so name
arguments.expected: after module_build, refl_describe_component shows the new components (recipe new-component-live step 3)
arguments.actual: rebuilt:true reloaded:true, the log says loaded glowmoth v1 from build/libglowmoth_loaded_5270_0.so each time (same name as the first load), and refl_describe_component Moth says unknown component; entity_create with the new components fails
arguments.workaround: trying to force the server off the cached copy name; otherwise the server has to be restarted
arguments.details: dlopen of a path already loaded returns the old image (a module with STB_GNU_UNIQUE symbols never unloads), so the copy needs a fresh name per reload
